questions.note: Order reads right: hallux longest, toe 2 a few mm shorter, 3–5 descending, and the hallux is broad and well padded. But toe 5 sits beside toe 4 at the same level with its nail facing up, neither rolled 35–40° nor tucked under (V5f, hr.lesser), and toes 2–5 are smooth tubes with ball knuckles, almost no PIP/DIP wrinkles, no redness, no corn on toe 4.

Five plates, none floating; the hallux free edge shows ~1 mm thickness, edges trimmed straight. But every plate is one opaque pale pink with a bright white free-edge stripe (a French pedicure at native size, V1f/V5f); the hallux has a glaring white band across its base, not a soft lunula; no cuticle, no folds lapping the plates, no pink bed; 3–5 are one outline scaled.

Veins now exist as relief (dorsal arch, tributaries, great saphenous in front of the medial malleolus in V2) and catch the light, but render paler than the skin: whitish even-width cords like scars or piping. The extensors are 6+ thin pale strings of equal strength in the same tone; the EHL does not dominate; no tibialis anterior at the ankle front.

SSS is restrained: toe shadow sides stay dark and nothing glows. But at closeup the skin is smooth cast silicone: no cell network, pores or fine lines on the dorsum and toes, one even peach with no redness at the knuckles; the ball's ridges are uniform corduroy, every pad carries the same target whorl with a seam, and the nails shine like acrylic.

defects.what: The great saphenous in front of the medial malleolus and the dorsal arch render paler than the skin: whitish, even-width, crisp-edged cords like scars or silicone piping laid on top; in V1f the arch crosses the medial border like a rubber band.
defects.fix: Superficial veins read darker and cooler than the skin: tint the vein mask toward grey-green #7d8b86 at about 18 %, vary the width 2.5–3.5 mm, feather the relief into the skin.

defects.what: Nails 3–5 are one rounded tombstone outline scaled down, each the same opaque pale pink with the same thin bright-white free-edge stripe: a French pedicure, visible at native size in V1f and V5f.
defects.fix: Give each nail its own outline and curvature; make the 4th and 5th smaller, thicker, duller and ridged, part-hidden by the lateral folds; translucent off-white free edges, uneven, with grime beneath.

defects.what: The hallux nail is a glossy milky-pink tile set in a groove: a bright white band across its whole base (brighter than the free edge), no cuticle on the plate, lateral folds not lapping its sides, no pink bed or onychodermal band, a clean plastic-cut edge.
defects.fix: Eponychium adherent 1–2 mm onto the plate, lateral folds overlapping its sides, a small off-white lunula crescent partly under the fold, pink bed through a satin, faintly yellow plate, a pale onychodermal band, an uneven edge with grime under it.

defects.what: From the medial side the plantar border skims only 2–4 mm above the floor from heel to ball (by eye at ~6 px/mm) and the instep is a near-straight ramp: a collapsed medial arch, a flat foot's profile.
defects.fix: Lift the medial longitudinal arch so a clear window shows under the navicular between heel pad and ball, with the instep rising convex to the cuneiform peak; keep only the 2–3 mm weight-bearing drop.

defects.what: At 43 px/mm the hallux and toe skin is smooth, even cast silicone: no polygonal cell network, no follicle pits, no fine crisscross lines, the same peach right up to the nail folds; the IP carries only two faint creases.
defects.fix: Dorsal toe skin with 0.25–0.4 mm cells, follicle pits, 3–6 transverse wrinkles over each IP, redness at the nail folds and knuckles, a cool blue-grey cast on the hallux dorsum.

defects.what: The instep and metatarsal dorsum carry no hair at all, none even in silhouette in V2 and V3; only the toe bases have a few strokes, so the foot reads shaved. §1.4 asks for 90–160 dark hairs lying toward the toes.
defects.fix: Scatter 90–160 terminal hairs (2 ± 1 per cm², 6–10 mm, radius 0.035 to 0.02 mm, dark brown) lying flat toward the toes with 10–20° yaw, thinning out by 55 % of the length.

defects.what: Six or more thin (1–2 mm), pale, evenly spaced ridges run to the toes at equal strength and in the same tone as the veins, like wires under the skin; the EHL is no stronger than the slips to toes 2–5.
defects.fix: One clear EHL cord to the hallux (5 mm wide, 1.5 proud) and four softer EDL slips (3.5 wide, 1.0 proud) fading toward the MTPs at rest; skin-coloured relief only.

defects.what: The ankle sits too far back: the medial malleolus apex is about 60 mm ahead of the pternion (V2, by eye at ~6 px/mm, allowing for perspective), not 73; the lateral about 51 mm in V3, not 60. The heel behind the ankle reads short.
defects.fix: Place the malleolar apexes 73 mm (medial) and 60 mm (lateral) ahead of the pternion, the joint centre at 68, keeping L = 282 mm; confirm with measure().

defects.what: From behind the ankle is still a broad smooth column with only a faint central crease and a medial shadow: no 16 mm Achilles cord narrowing into the heel, no retro-malleolar hollows either side.
defects.fix: A raised Achilles cord 16 × 7 mm at z 100 narrowing to its insertion, with 4 mm deep hollows between it and each malleolus.

defects.what: Toe 5 lies beside toe 4 at the same level with a gap between them and its nail facing up like the others: it is neither rolled 35–40° nor tucked under toe 4.
defects.fix: Roll toe 5 about 40° so its nail faces up and out, and draw it in under toe 4's lateral side, closing the 4–5 cleft.

defects.what: Toes 2–5 are smooth glossy tubes: ball-like PIP knuckles with a few faint strokes, no DIP creases, no redness or thickened skin over the joints, no corn on toe 4's PIP, soft rubbery pulps.
defects.fix: 3–6 transverse wrinkles 0.2 mm deep over each PIP and DIP, redder skin on the knuckles, the 5 mm dorsal corn on toe 4 (#e6d0a4 with a #c9ad8a ring), drier, flatter tips.

defects.what: Only the heel rim has callus: the ball under MT heads 1–2 is smooth pink, and there is no callus on the lateral 5th MTP or the medial hallux IP and no corn on toe 4 (V3, hr.hallux, hr.lesser).
defects.fix: Add the three missing callus zones and the corn at §3.4's places and sizes: paler and yellower (#e0cba8), rougher, ridges flattened, edges soft.

defects.what: The heel-rim callus is an even mesh of fine dark polygons like crackle glaze, its top edge dusted with white speckles like salt, its lower part a dirty grey-green: it reads as grime or a decal, not thick dry skin.
defects.fix: Thick, dry, yellow-white skin fading in over 5–10 mm, a few longer fissures running across the rim, fine scaling; no even polygon mesh, no speckled edge, no green.

defects.what: No 5th metatarsal styloid: the lateral border is a smooth curve where §3.2 puts an 8 mm bump 2.5 mm proud at (+50, -150, 18); V4's lateral outline is smooth there too.
defects.fix: Add the styloid 150 mm ahead of the pternion on the lateral border, 8 mm across and 2.5 mm proud, the peroneus brevis line running into it.

defects.what: The lateral malleolus is a soft low swelling with no bony edge, no hollow in front of it and none between it and the Achilles: the outside of the ankle reads padded.
defects.fix: A distinct bony knob, 24 mm across and 5 mm proud, pointed below, with the sinus-tarsi hollow in front and the retro-malleolar hollow behind.

defects.what: No tibialis anterior at the front of the ankle and no anterior ankle crease: the shin runs into the instep in one smooth concave curve; on a lean man the TA stands out as a cord to the medial cuneiform.
defects.fix: Add the TA cord (9 mm wide, 1.5 proud) from (-22, -75, 80) to (-30, -135, 55) and the ankle crease with 2–3 fine lines above it.

defects.what: The ball and the toes' undersides carry one field of parallel horizontal ridges, the same pitch, depth and direction everywhere, like corduroy; no ball crease, no flow around the MT heads.
defects.fix: Ridges that flow in curved fields around the MT heads with deltas and minutiae, flattened where the ball takes weight, crossed by the curved ball crease and fine creases.

defects.what: Every toe pad carries the same perfect concentric-oval target, and a straight radial seam runs into the whorl centre (hallux shown, toe 3 the same) with the ridges mismatched across it.
defects.fix: Loops and whorls that differ toe to toe, with deltas, bifurcations and ridge endings, continuous across the pad, no seam.

defects.what: Toe 3's PIP crease and toe 4's basal crease are ruler-straight hairlines with a tone step and a jog in the outline, a seam between two pieces rather than a soft flexion fold.
defects.fix: Digital flexion creases 0.5 mm deep, gently curved and often doubled, with the ridges running into them and the skin bulging softly either side.

defects.what: The toe hairs are a few short, dead-straight, near-vertical dark dashes, like scratches, not fine hairs curving and lying flat toward the tips.
defects.fix: Hallux tuft of 8–12 hairs 5–8 mm and 2–4 hairs 3–6 mm on toes 2–4, curved, lying flat toward the tips with random yaw, tapering to fine ends.

ranked: [D1] The veins are the loudest tell now: the great saphenous and the dorsal arch are paler than the skin, whitish piping laid on the foot. Real superficial veins read darker and cooler, blue-grey-green, and melt into the skin at their edges.

[D2] At native size every nail wears a bright white free-edge stripe on an opaque pale-pink plate, a French pedicure, and 3–5 are one outline scaled. A soldier's lesser nails differ toe to toe: duller, ridged, part-hidden by their folds, grime under the edge.
[D3] The hallux nail is a glossy acrylic tile set in a groove, with a glaring white band across its base, no cuticle, no folds lapping its sides and no pink bed showing through the plate.

[D4] From the medial side the foot is flat: the plantar border skims 2–4 mm above the floor from heel to ball and the instep is a straight ramp. A fit soldier's foot shows a clear arch window under the navicular.

[D5] The skin is smooth cast silicone at every closeup: no cell network, pores or fine lines, one peach everywhere, no redness at the knuckles or nail folds. A 40-year-old's foot is drier, finer-textured and zoned in colour.
Overall the foot reads young, clean and manicured: no dryness, no darker skin in the creases, no dirt at the nail edges, no marks of boots. It is a mannequin's foot more than a 40-year-old soldier's.
[D6] The instep and metatarsal dorsum are bare, so the foot looks shaved; men's feet, as in the anchor photos, carry sparse dark hairs lying toward the toes.
[D7] The extensors are a fan of thin pale strings of equal strength in the same tone as the veins; at rest a real EHL is one soft dominant cord and the slips to toes 2–5 fade before the knuckles.

[D8] The ankle sits too far back on the foot: the malleolar apexes measure about 60 mm (medial) and 51 mm (lateral) ahead of the pternion against §3.2's 73 and 60, so the heel behind the ankle reads short.
[D9] From behind, the ankle is still a smooth column with a faint central crease: no Achilles cord narrowing into the heel and no hollows beside it.
[D10] Toe 5 stands beside toe 4 as a small separate toe with its nail facing up; in a boot-wearer it rolls outward and tucks partly under toe 4.
[D11] Toes 2–5 are smooth glossy tubes with ball knuckles, almost no wrinkles over the PIP or DIP, no redness and no corn; boot-worn toes show creased, reddened, thickened knuckle skin.
[D12] Only the heel rim carries callus: the ball under MT heads 1–2, the lateral 5th MTP and the medial hallux IP are as smooth and pink as the arch, and toe 4 has no corn.
[D13] The heel-rim callus is an even crackle-glaze mesh with a salt-speckled top edge and a grey-green lower band, so it reads as grime or a decal rather than thick dry skin.
[D14] No 5th metatarsal styloid: the lateral border is a smooth curve where one of the foot's most visible bony landmarks should bump out.
[D15] The lateral malleolus is a soft swelling with no hollow in front of it or behind it; the outside of the ankle reads padded, not bony.
[D16] No tibialis anterior cord and no anterior ankle crease at the front of the ankle; the shin flows into the instep in one smooth curve.
[D17] The ball and toe undersides are covered in uniform horizontal ridges like corduroy, with no ball crease and no flow around the metatarsal heads.
[D18] Every toe pad wears the same concentric target with a straight seam running into its centre; real pads carry loops and whorls that differ toe to toe.
[D19] The plantar creases on toes 3 and 4 are ruler-straight hairlines with a tone step, so from below the toes look like segments joined at seams.
[D20] The few toe hairs are short, straight, near-vertical dashes like scratches, not fine curved hairs lying toward the tips.
Detail is uneven: the sole and pads carry crisp ridges at 20 px/mm while the dorsal skin beside them is blank, so the underside looks textured and the top airbrushed.
